title: `default_discipline is exercised as a WORKING directive in the chapter that forbids it
detail: C.4 bullet 3: "the `default_discipline compiler directive is not supported in Verilog-A. All Verilog-A modules shall have a discipline defined for each module." 09_default_discipline_current_behavior.va puts `default_discipline electrical on line 11 and is a RUN fixture; because it also declares `electrical p, n` explicitly the directive binds nothing, and the two CHECKX values (V(p)=1.25, V(p,n)=1.0) are plain 5.4.1 probe facts that hold whether or not the directive is supported. A compiler that implements the forbidden directive passes; a compiler that rejects it also passes the physics but fails the build. VERIFIED: a module with no explicit discipline and only `default_discipline electrical compiles clean through zig-out/bin/vera --lint (rc=0, no diagnostic), so the rule is unenforced. The literals lens independently confirms both numbers are arithmetically right but unreachable on a conforming compiler. Rewrite: delete the explicit `electrical p, n` so the directive is the only source of a discipline, delete both CHECKX lines, and demand the diagnostic.
expected: //! lrm C.4 + //! lrm 3.8 + //! reject default_discipline + //! xfail (VerA implements the directive in ch10 and has no Verilog-A subset gate). Prefer a dedicated E03xx code once one exists; the substring travels meanwhile. Rename off the _current_behavior suffix and add the .expected-error.txt.

title: 18_no_discipline_analog_net.va asserts VerA's implicit-electrical fallback as if it were the LRM
detail: C.4: "All Verilog-A modules shall have a discipline defined for each module." The fixture declares `inout p;` with no discipline and then asserts CHECKX(V(p), 0.25) — its own header admits this "records what VerA does". With no discipline there is no nature, hence no `V` access function, hence no 0.25: the number is not derivable from the LRM, so a CONFORMING compiler fails this fixture and a non-conforming one passes it. VERIFIED: `module m(p); inout p; analog I(p) <+ V(p); endmodule` compiles clean (rc=0). Both the weak and literals lenses flag the same over-specification. Rewrite as a reject.
expected: //! lrm C.4 + //! reject (a diagnostic naming the missing discipline) + //! xfail. No CHECKs — the value 0.25 must go, it is the implementation's fallback and not a rule.

title: The annex's only literal "shall be an error" is a fixture that asserts nothing and never runs
detail: 07_discrete_discipline_current_behavior.va has no //! reject, no CHECK, and an empty portless module — torture.zig classifies it CANNOT RUN (refusedByContract: num_ports is 0, tests/torture.zig:798) and conformance.zig only requires that it compile. It proves nothing. IMPORTANT CORRECTION to the lens proposals: what it contains is a discipline DEFINITION, and C.17 explicitly says an implementation "shall silently ignore any definition of a discipline with a domain of discrete" — that case is already covered, correctly, by tests/fixtures/annex_d_standard_definitions/discrete_disciplines.va, which compiles clean. Turning a bare definition into an error would contradict a passing fixture. C.4's error is about 3.6.2.2 domain BINDING, so the fixture must bind a net: VERIFIED that `ddiscrete q;` (and `logic q;`) from the annex D prelude — src/frontend/preprocessor.zig:1043-1049 defines both with `domain discrete` — declares a discrete-domain net inside a Verilog-A module and compiles clean, rc=0. No fixture in the entire tree binds a net to a discrete-domain discipline.
expected: Keep the discrete discipline DEFINITION legal (C.17). Add a port list plus `ddiscrete q;` as a net declaration and demand the C.4 error: //! lrm C.4 + //! lrm 3.6.2.2 + //! reject + //! xfail. Leave annex_d_standard_definitions/discrete_disciplines.va alone as the C.17 silent-ignore side of the boundary.

title: A conformant wreal rejection is filed as VerA DEBT, so the ledger counts a pass as a defect
detail: 08_wreal_current_behavior.va opens with "DEBT — this rejection is NOT conformance. The LRM permits what VerA refuses here" and cites VAMS-3.7-01..03 from Clause 3. That header is false in THIS chapter and for THIS compiler: README.md line 3 states VerA is "A Verilog-A compiler", and C.4 bullet 2 says "the wreal data type is not supported in Verilog-A", which removes Clause 3.7 from the subset by name. The E0205/wreal rejection is therefore exactly right, and `zig build ledger` is currently scoring a conformance pass against the compiler. Only the header, the three VAMS-3.7 quotes and the filename need to change — the reject lines and the .expected-error.txt are correct as they stand.
expected: Delete the DEBT block and the VAMS-3.7 quotes, add //! lrm C.4, rename to 08_wreal_rejected.va (with the matching .expected-error.txt). Keep //! reject E0205 and //! reject wreal.

title: The suite states as conformance that a Verilog-A module may not instantiate a child
detail: C.8: "The hierarchical structure defined in Clause 6 is applicable to both Verilog-AMS HDL and Verilog-A, except support for real value ports is only applicable to Verilog-AMS HDL (see 6.5.3)." Clause 6 hierarchy is INSIDE the subset with exactly one carve-out. annex_a_syntax/11_module_instantiation_rejected.va instantiates `annex_a_child child_instance(p, n);` and carries a bare `//! reject E0204` with no //! xfail and no cite, so the suite asserts the rejection as correct behaviour. It is a VerA limitation, not a rule. This is the single largest anti-conformance the Annex C audit surfaces; it lives in another chapter's directory but it is C.8 that makes it wrong.
expected: Add //! lrm C.8 and //! xfail ("VerA does not implement module instantiation; Clause 6 hierarchy is in the Verilog-A subset per C.8") to the annex_a fixture. Optionally add a positive annex_c run fixture instantiating a child, also xfail, so C.8's inclusion is stated somewhere in this chapter. Do not touch the real-value-port carve-out, which is C-11 below.

title: `net_resolution` is in the C.16 list, is missing from the fixture, and is not reserved by VerA
detail: C.16 lists ten keywords not used by Verilog-A: connect connectmodule connectrules driver_update endconnectrules merged net_resolution resolvedto split wreal. 16_unused_ams_words_current_behavior.va inventories nine of them and omits net_resolution. VERIFIED: `real net_resolution;` compiles clean through vera --lint (rc=0); grep finds net_resolution nowhere in src/ or tests/, and src/frontend/token.zig:596-598 lists the other nine but not it. NOTE — one lens sub-claim DROPPED: the fixture's `resolveto` is CORRECT, not a typo. Annex B (normative, docs/VAMS-LRM/annex-b-keywords.html:103) prints `resolveto` and separately lists `net_resolution` at line 69; C.16's `resolvedto` is the LRM's own typo. Confirmed empirically: `real resolvedto;` compiles and should. Secondary point: 16 puts nine words on two lines, compilation stops at `connect`, so the other eight are never reached — only one word is actually proven reserved by the suite (all nine are in fact in token.zig, so this is a proof gap, not a compiler gap).
expected: New one-word fixture `real net_resolution;` with //! lrm C.16 + //! lrm B + //! reject E0208 + //! xfail (token.zig does not reserve it). Fix is one string in src/frontend/token.zig:597. Optionally split 16 into one word per fixture so all ten are provable; leave `resolveto` exactly as it is.

title: casex/casez pin the bare word "expression" while E0416, written for this exact rule, is dead code
detail: C.7: "casex and casez are not supported in Verilog-A." 11 and 12 both carry `//! reject expression` and an .expected-error.txt of one word. VERIFIED: the real diagnostic is E0209 "expected an expression: found `casex`" — a parser-recovery message about A.8.3, not the C.7 rule; a compiler could emit it for a hundred unrelated inputs. Meanwhile src/diag_code.zig:1388 defines E0416 "casex/casez are not in the analog subset" with .lrm = "C.7", and src/ir/lower.zig:2011 is the only site that raises it — unreachable, because src/frontend/parser.zig:908-916 deliberately does not dispatch casex/casez and parser.zig:2459-2460 asserts E0209 as the intended answer, so Ast.CaseKind (ast.zig:714) is never anything but .normal.
expected: Minimum: //! lrm C.7 + //! reject E0209 on both 11 and 12, so the code is pinned rather than a message fragment. Better: dispatch casex/casez in parseStmt so E0416 fires, then pin E0416 — the code already carries the C.7 cite. Either way flag lower.zig:2011 as dead or wire it up.

title: No Annex C fixture for @(posedge)/@(negedge) in an analog block; the only sibling calls its own rejection non-conformant
detail: C.7: "No digital behavior or events are supported in Verilog-A." No fixture in annex_c_analog_subset uses posedge or negedge. The only coverage in the tree is ch07_mixed_signal/digital_event_unsupported.va, which is headed "DEBT — this rejection is NOT conformance" — true for Verilog-AMS, exactly inverted for the Verilog-A subset this chapter tests. VERIFIED: `analog begin @(posedge s) s = 1; ... end` is rejected with E0209 "expected an expression: found posedge", so this fixture passes today and needs no xfail.
expected: New reject fixture, both edges, //! lrm C.7 + //! reject E0209. States the rejection as conformance in the chapter where it is conformance, without disturbing the ch07 DEBT framing which is correct for Clause 7.

title: Nonblocking `<=` inside an analog block has no fixture
detail: C.7 excludes digital behavior; 5.6/A.6.4 give the analog block only `=` and `<+`. NARROWED from the negatives lens, whose claim of "zero coverage anywhere in the tree" is FALSE — tests/fixtures/ch08_scheduling/nonblocking_unsupported.va exists. But that fixture writes `always @(source) target <= source;`, so what it actually rejects is `always`; the nonblocking operator inside an `analog` block is untested. VERIFIED: `analog begin s <= 1; ... end` is rejected with E0214 "expected '<+' or '=': found ';'", cite LRM 5.6. Passes today.
expected: New reject fixture with `<=` in an analog block, //! lrm C.7 + //! lrm 5.6 + //! reject E0214. No xfail.

title: The digital continuous `assign` has no Annex C fixture; its only sibling confounds it with wreal and calls it debt
detail: C.7 excludes digital behavior. The only `assign` coverage is ch07_mixed_signal/continuous_assign_unsupported.va, which declares `wreal out;` in the same module, pins three substrings at once (E0205, wreal, assign) so no single rule is isolated, and is headed "DEBT — this rejection is NOT conformance". VERIFIED: a module with `wire w; assign w = 1'b1;` and an otherwise clean analog block is rejected with E0205 "unsupported module item: found assign", cite A.1.4. Passes today.
expected: New reject fixture with `assign` and no wreal, //! lrm C.7 + //! reject E0205 + //! reject assign. Isolates the construct so the diagnostic can only be about `assign`.

title: The one true C.8 carve-out is pinned on the bare word "identifier" and tests only `input real`
detail: C.8: real value ports are the single Clause 6 construct excluded from Verilog-A (see 6.5.3), so this rejection IS conformance and is the most valuable reject in the chapter. It is pinned on the substring "identifier". VERIFIED: the real diagnostic is E0208 "expected an identifier: found `real`" with note LRM 2.8 — a lexical recovery message, not the 6.5.3 rule; and only the `input` direction is covered, not `output real` or `inout real`.
expected: //! lrm C.8 + //! lrm 6.5.3 + //! reject E0208, and add output/inout arms (separate fixtures, or one file per direction since compilation stops at the first). Passes today, no xfail.

title: 19 pins only a phase label, and contradicts ch05 on whether named events are in the subset
detail: 19_digital_event_trigger.va pins the single substring "DiagnosticsReported", which is a torture.zig PHASE LABEL (tests/torture.zig:617) and pins no rule at all — every rejected fixture in the suite reports it. VERIFIED the file produces two diagnostics: E0203 "named event declaration is not implemented" on `event tick;` (cite 5.10.4) and E0209 on `-> tick`, so the second construct the header cares about is masked by the first. Worse, the premise is contested: tests/fixtures/ch05_analog_behavior/named_event_unsupported.va argues at length that named events ARE in the Verilog-A subset (5.10 lists named events as the third kind of ANALOG event; C.2 lists events as a Verilog-A feature; C.7 excludes DIGITAL events) and marks the same E0203 as a VerA limitation. Confirmed against the LRM: 5.10.4 sits inside 5.10 Analog events and says named events can be triggered "from always and initial blocks, or from an analog event statement". One of the two fixtures is wrong; 19 is the weaker-reasoned one.
expected: Adopt ch05's reading: rename off "digital", //! lrm 5.10.4 + //! reject E0203 + //! xfail (VerA does not implement named events). Split the `-> tick` trigger into its own fixture so it is not masked by the declaration error, or drop it. If instead the suite decides named events are out of the subset, ch05_analog_behavior/named_event_unsupported.va must change and its long justification must be deleted — do not leave both.

title: No Annex C fixture rejects a connect-rule CONSTRUCT as out of subset — only the keywords as identifiers
detail: C.9: "Clause 7 only applies to Verilog-AMS HDL", and C.16 lists connect/connectmodule/connectrules/endconnectrules as unused by Verilog-A. COVERAGE.md's own disposition for C.9 is the bare phrase "no mixed-signal valid fixture". 16_unused_ams_words proves only that `connect` cannot be an identifier; nothing asserts that a `connectrules ... endconnectrules` block or a `connectmodule` declaration is refused as a construct. The existing ch07_mixed_signal/resolution_connect_unsupported.va is in the AMS chapter, where the construct is legal.
expected: One reject fixture containing a connectrules block (and/or a connectmodule declaration) with //! lrm C.9 + //! lrm C.16 + //! reject. Check the actual code before pinning; the keywords lex to .kw_reserved so it will most likely be E0205 or E0208.

title: COVERAGE.md is the source of the chapter's anti-conformance framing, and three of its rows are factually stale
detail: Eight rows describe fixtures as "snapshot the three missing exclusion diagnostics", "expose current acceptance", "snapshots the current missing-discipline acceptance gap", "snapshots the current reservation gap", "records the real-port parser rejection" — the vocabulary that produced C-01..C-04. Three are VERIFIED STALE against the shipped binary: the C.5 row claims 10 and 17 "expose current acceptance of === and !==" but `===` is rejected today with E0323 "case equality is not in the analog subset"; the C.16 row claims 16 "snapshots the current reservation gap" but `connect` is rejected today with E0208. The C.16 row also reproduces the nine-word list and so inherits the missing `net_resolution` (C-06). The C.8 row says "hierarchy is deliberately rejected by Annex A's instantiation fixture", which is the C-05 defect written down as policy. The C.9 row's disposition is "no mixed-signal valid fixture" with no reject either (C-13).
expected: Rewrite every row as the requirement it pins, not as a description of VerA's state. Rows to correct: C.4 (three real exclusions, now rejects), C.5 (already conformant — drop "current acceptance"), C.6 (18 becomes a reject), C.8 (hierarchy is IN the subset; only real-value ports are out), C.9 (name the new reject), C.16 (ten words incl. net_resolution; keep `resolveto`, note C.16's `resolvedto` is an LRM typo against normative Annex B), C.17 (point at annex_d_standard_definitions/discrete_disciplines.va for silent-ignore).

title: Zero //! lrm cites exist in the chapter, and three filenames still claim to snapshot behaviour that is already conformant
detail: VERIFIED by reading all 19 .va files: not one carries a //! lrm line, so `zig build torture -- --coverage` (tests/torture.zig:365) reports nothing for Annex C and no reject in the chapter is traceable to a clause. All 11 reject fixtures need one: 06 (C.3, 2.6), 08 (C.4), 10 and 17 (C.5), 11 and 12 (C.7), 13 and 14 (C.7), 15 (C.8, 6.5.3), 16 (C.16, Annex B), 19 (5.10.4). Folded in: three files are named *_current_behavior.va but are correct, passing conformance rejects — 08_wreal (see C-04), 10_case_equality (E0323 fires), 16_unused_ams_words (E0208 fires). The names are the last trace of the snapshot framing.
expected: One sweep: add the //! lrm line to all 11 rejects; rename 10_case_equality_current_behavior.va and 16_unused_ams_words_current_behavior.va (08 is renamed by C-04) together with their .expected-error.txt files and their COVERAGE.md rows. No behavioural change, no new fixtures.

title: `?` as the alternative for the z digit is a separate C.3 sentence with no fixture
detail: C.3, second sentence of the 2.6 bullet: "In the same paragraph, the use of the question mark character as an alternative for z is also limited to the mixed signal context." 06_xz_rejected.va covers `4'b0x1z` only. VERIFIED: `4'b01?1` is already rejected with E0130 "x/z digit in a number literal", note LRM 2.6.1, so this passes today and costs one line or one small sibling fixture.
expected: Add a `?`-digit literal arm — a sibling 06b/26 fixture is cleaner than a second literal in the same file, since compilation stops at the first. //! lrm C.3 + //! lrm 2.6.1 + //! reject E0130.

title: fork/join, wait, disable, deassign, release and user `task` have no Annex C fixture
detail: C.7 excludes digital behavior wholesale. 13 and 14 cover `initial` and `always`; the rest of the family is covered only by cross-chapter megafixtures (annex_b_keywords/10_task_control_keywords.va and friends) pinned on ParseError, plus ch08_scheduling files whose headers frame the rejection as a scheduler limitation. All of these words are in src/frontend/token.zig's reserved list so the rejections exist; only the Annex C statement of them is missing. Lowest value in the chapter — the constructs are unambiguously refused, this is bookkeeping.
expected: One fixture per construct is overkill; a small set (fork/join, wait, disable) with //! lrm C.7 and the code pinned is enough. Verify each code before writing — do not reuse ParseError.

title: CHECKI(state, 0) is satisfied by a compiler that drops the event bodies entirely
detail: `integer state;` starts at 0, `@(initial_step) state = 0;` writes 0, and the assertion checks 0 — so the check passes whether the events ran or not. The intent (5.10.3.1: cross(expr,+1) must NOT fire at a DC point with no history) is real, and the companion `seen` variable already covers initial_step correctly (3 before, 5 after). Only the cross half is soft. Weakest of the four valid fixtures; 01-04 are sound and all 13 literals in the chapter were independently recomputed and are correct.
expected: Seed a distinguishable value: `state = 7;` before the events, keep `@(initial_step) state = 0;`, keep CHECKI(state, 0). Then a dropped initial_step reads 7 and a spuriously-fired cross reads 1. One line.
